steps.text: Steam's own CEF interface hangs under msync/esync, but GAMES gain ~40% frame rate from msync. Wine's sync mode is fixed when the prefix's wineserver starts, so: the bottle runs msync (games, silent -applaunch sessions), and the Steam UI pin carries WINEMSYNC=0/WINEESYNC=0 for its own cold starts. Highball's app restarts the wineserver when you open the Steam window. Verified 2026-08-24 on M1 Pro / macOS 14.6.

steps.label: SteamSetup
steps.slow: Steam's installer is quick, but its first launch afterwards downloads and unpacks the full client — 15 to 25 minutes that can look frozen. Let it finish; it resumes if it crashes.

steps.text: First launch downloads the 64-bit client (~235 MB) and extracts it. Under WoW64 + Rosetta the 32-bit bootstrapper takes 15–25 minutes and may look frozen; let it finish. If it crashes with 'nested exception on signal stack', relaunch — it resumes.
In Steam: Settings → Interface → disable 'GPU accelerated rendering in web views'; Settings → In-Game → disable the Steam Overlay. Both are unstable under Wine.

knownIssues.symptom: Steam window opened after playing a game shows no UI
knownIssues.cause: wineserver still running in msync from the game session
knownIssues.fix: stop the bottle's processes first (the Highball app does this automatically)

err:virtual:virtual_setup_exception nested exception on signal stack during first update
knownIssues.cause: 32-bit bootstrapper under experimental WoW64 (seen with msync+DXMT)
knownIssues.fix: relaunch; the update resumes from package/
